examFacts.answer: The Water Regulations certificate shows a plumber knows the Water Supply (Water Fittings) Regulations 1999 in England and Wales, and the matching Scottish Byelaws 2014 and Northern Ireland 2009 Regulations: what must be notified to the water company, the five fluid categories, which backflow device or air gap suits each, and the Schedule 2 rules for pipework, cisterns, hot water, WCs and taps. Awarding bodies such as City & Guilds and BPEC run it as an open-book multiple-choice test after a short course, and it is the usual evidence for joining an approved contractors' scheme.

landing.studyHeading: How to Pass the Water Regulations Test
tips: Know the five fluid categories cold

Most backflow questions start from the fluid category: drinking water is 1, aesthetic changes 2, slight hazard 3, significant hazard 4 and serious hazard 5. Learn an example of each, then the devices allowed for each category.
Know which jobs need the water company's consent before work starts, how much notice is needed, and which jobs an approved contractor can do without notifying.
Use the open book, but do not rely on it

The test is open book, but there is not time to look up every answer. Tab the fluid category tables and the backflow device schedule, and know the common figures (test pressures, temperatures, WC flush volumes) without looking.
Tigertest tracks your accuracy by topic. Aim for 90 percent on every practice test before the real one, so you have room above the 80 percent line.
faqs: Is the Water Regulations test open book?

Yes. City & Guilds lets candidates take the Water Regulations Guide into the 3345 test, and BPEC allows its training manual and course notes. You still need to know where things are, because there is not time to look up every answer.
What pass mark do I need?

BPEC's Water Regulations and Byelaws test needs 42 of 52 (80%), with a second attempt on the missed questions if you score 37 to 41. City & Guilds does not publish its mark. Tigertest uses 80% as the line.
Does this cover Scotland and Northern Ireland?

The questions follow the 1999 Regulations for England and Wales. Scotland's Byelaws 2014 and Northern Ireland's 2009 Regulations are almost the same; where they differ, such as the 20°C cold water limit and notifying Scottish Water or NI Water, the question says so.
Does passing make me an approved plumber?

No. The certificate is the evidence most approved contractors' schemes ask for, but you join a scheme (WIAPS, APHC, CIPHE or SNIPEF) separately. Approved contractors can skip notifying some jobs and issue compliance certificates.
Is the new backflow specification included?

Defra published a new Specification on the Prevention of Backflow on 6 May 2026, which takes effect on 6 May 2027. The device types and fluid categories asked here are the same in both; the new Type AUK4 air gap for WC suites is left out until it is in force.
